author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A five-page scanned letter in which PKD discusses his own craft and working method, one of the archive's undated items preserving his reflections on how his fiction gets made.
page_summary:
This is a five-page archived letter in which Philip K. Dick turns to the subject of writing itself. The specific recipient and date are not established in the archive record, but the letter belongs to the large body of correspondence in which PKD, an unusually self-analytic novelist, described how his books came together, what he was trying to do with them, and how he understood his own methods.

PKD wrote about his craft throughout his life, in letters to editors, scholars, and fellow writers, and such letters are a standard source for his ideas about science fiction, the shaping of a plot, and the pressures of writing fast for paperback markets.

The entry preserves the scanned document as a discrete archive item; its documentary value lies in giving a first-person account of PKD's practice in his own words.
